citacoes.trecho: This paper presents a systematic prompt ablation study across three real-world REST API coding tasks—user registration, password reset, and product search—comparing Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-4o.
Each task was decomposed into six semantic components: (C1) functional core, (C2) security, (C3) validation, (C4) error handling, (C5) HTTP conventions, (C6) REST conventions.
Seven variants were generated: full baseline (v0), five single-component ablations (v1–v5), and bare minimum (v6, C1 only).
Ablating a component tests whether the model generates the corresponding feature implicitly.
Both models were accessed via their respective APIs on 15 March 2026, using model identifiers claude-sonnet-4-6 and gpt-4o with a maximum token limit of 1500 and default temperature settings.
In Task 1 GPT-4o v2 stored the raw password with no hashing, no warning (Type 3).
In Task 2 GPT-4o v2 stored the raw token with no warning.
In Task 3, both models used parameterised queries despite security instruction being absent (Type 1).
This repeatability check addresses a known concern in LLM-based studies that non-deterministic outputs may undermine the reliability of single-run observations [13].
Based on our observations, security instructions should be made explicit when using GPT-4o — omitting them produced silent dangerous degradation without warning in two of three tasks studied

Manual validation of all 42 artifacts was performed to mitigate this risk; future work should employ an independent judge model or human annotators with inter-rater agreement to address this limitation more rigorously.
In our study, bare minimum prompts produced model-specific schemas — explicit field specifications may be needed for consistent cross-model output across similar tasks
Repeatability was assessed on Task 1 only; stability rates may differ across tasks, particularly for features that showed greater score variation in the ablation results.
Claude exhibits proactive security (Type 2) across all 3 tasks; GPT-4o exhibits silent degradation (Type 3) in Tasks 1 and 2
Security feature scores v0 → v2 (−Security). Claude degrades gracefully or holds (Type 2); GPT-4o drops silently to ABSENT in Tasks 1 and 2 (Type 3).
Note: Task 2 κ = 0.22 despite 81.2% raw agreement because 77% of cells were PRESENT for both models, inflating Pe = 0.72.
Three independent Claude runs on Task 1 v6: 13/14 features (92.9%) stable, 95% Wilson CI [68.5%, 98.7%].
